units.title: English Literature: Shakespeare
units.description: Analyse character, theme, language and dramatic methods in an original short Shakespearean-style extract and contextual summary.
units.generationNotes: Do not reproduce copyrighted play text. Use public-domain or original paraphrased micro-extracts and clearly separate evidence from context.

objectives.text: Analyse how Shakespeare presents characters, themes and ideas through language, form and structure.

units.title: English Literature: nineteenth-century novel
units.description: Explore character, setting, theme and social context in nineteenth-century fiction using concise original or public-domain examples.
units.generationNotes: No long quotations. Use short public-domain excerpts or paraphrase and require evidence-based interpretation.

objectives.text: Analyse nineteenth-century prose using evidence, context and the writer's methods.

units.title: English Literature: modern prose or drama
units.description: Compare ideas, characters and methods in modern prose or drama without relying on an unseen copyrighted text.
units.generationNotes: Use original fictional examples or brief paraphrase. Do not name a single set text as universal; teach transferable analysis.

objectives.text: Analyse modern prose or drama using evidence, structure, language and context.

units.title: English Literature: poetry comparison
units.description: Compare poetic ideas, imagery, voice and structure across themes such as power, conflict or relationships.
units.generationNotes: Use public-domain or original short poems; do not reproduce anthology poems. Teach comparison through precise evidence and method.

objectives.text: Compare poems using evidence and analysis of language, form, structure and context.

units.title: English Literature: unseen poetry
units.description: Approach an unfamiliar poem by identifying voice, imagery, structure and a defensible interpretation.
units.generationNotes: Use original short poems. Explain that interpretations need evidence and can differ when supported by the text.

objectives.text: Analyse an unseen poem and develop an evidence-supported interpretation.

units.title: Biology: cell biology
units.description: Understand cell structure, microscopy, transport and cell division through clear GCSE-level scientific reasoning.
units.generationNotes: Give all data and describe diagrams in words. Distinguish plant, animal and bacterial cells and avoid unsupported health claims.

objectives.text: Explain cell structures and processes including microscopy, transport and cell division.

units.title: Biology: organisation
units.description: Explain how cells form tissues, organs and systems, including digestion and enzyme action.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional data and fully stated conditions. Explain enzyme variables without giving medical advice.

objectives.text: Explain organisation in living organisms and apply knowledge to digestion and enzymes.

units.title: Biology: infection and response
units.description: Describe pathogens, barriers, immune responses, vaccination and antibiotic resistance with careful scientific language.
units.generationNotes: Use educational fictional scenarios, do not diagnose illness or recommend treatment. Distinguish viruses and bacteria and explain resistance accurately.

objectives.text: Explain how pathogens cause disease and how organisms and medicines respond.

units.title: Biology: bioenergetics
units.description: Explain photosynthesis, respiration, energy transfer and factors affecting rates using equations and data.
units.generationNotes: State equations and variables clearly. Use fictional experiment data and distinguish correlation from causation.

objectives.text: Explain photosynthesis and respiration and analyse factors affecting their rates.

units.title: Biology: homeostasis
units.description: Understand nervous and hormonal coordination and how organisms maintain stable internal conditions.
units.generationNotes: Use simplified fictional control-system examples; avoid medical diagnosis or personal health advice.

objectives.text: Explain homeostasis, coordination and the role of nervous and hormonal systems.

units.title: Biology: inheritance and evolution
units.description: Use DNA, genes, inheritance, variation, natural selection and classification to explain biological change.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional organisms and simple genetic examples. Explain probabilities carefully and avoid deterministic claims about people.

objectives.text: Explain inheritance, variation, evolution and classification using appropriate evidence.

units.title: Biology: ecology
units.description: Study ecosystems, interdependence, biodiversity and human effects on the environment using data and systems thinking.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional populations and clearly stated data. Distinguish a correlation from proof of cause.

objectives.text: Explain ecosystems, biodiversity and human impacts using ecological evidence.

units.title: Chemistry: atomic structure
units.description: Describe atoms, elements, compounds, isotopes and the periodic table using particle and electronic ideas.
units.generationNotes: Give all particle numbers in text. Use standard notation consistently and distinguish atoms, ions and molecules.

objectives.text: Use atomic structure and the periodic table to explain elements, isotopes and ions.

units.title: Chemistry: bonding and structure
units.description: Explain ionic, covalent and metallic bonding and relate structure to properties.
units.generationNotes: Describe structures in words where no diagram is supplied. Link properties to particles and forces without overgeneralising.

objectives.text: Explain bonding, structure and properties of substances.

units.title: Chemistry: quantitative chemistry
units.description: Use formulae, equations, relative masses, moles and concentration in fully specified calculations.
units.generationNotes: Show units and all given values. Use fictional substances and check significant figures; do not depend on an unseen periodic table.

objectives.text: Use chemical equations and quantitative methods to calculate amounts and concentrations.

units.title: Chemistry: chemical changes
units.description: Explain reactivity, acids, electrolysis and redox changes using particles, equations and observations.
units.generationNotes: Use safe fictional or classroom contexts and do not provide hazardous experimental instructions. State observations and conditions explicitly.

objectives.text: Explain chemical changes including reactivity, acids, electrolysis and redox.

units.title: Chemistry: energy changes
units.description: Describe exothermic and endothermic reactions and interpret simple energy profiles and data.
units.generationNotes: Give numerical data in the prompt. Distinguish energy transferred from temperature change and avoid unsafe practical directions.

objectives.text: Explain and interpret energy changes in chemical reactions.

units.title: Chemistry: rate of reaction
units.description: Explain collision theory and how concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts affect reaction rate.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional data and describe variables and controls. Do not imply that a correlation alone proves a mechanism.

objectives.text: Explain and analyse factors affecting reaction rates using collision theory.

units.title: Chemistry: organic chemistry
units.description: Recognise hydrocarbons, crude oil, polymers and common organic reactions at GCSE level.
units.generationNotes: Use text formulae and short chains. Avoid industrial safety claims and do not depend on structural diagrams that are not rendered.

objectives.text: Describe key organic substances, reactions and uses using appropriate formulae.

units.title: Chemistry: chemical analysis
units.description: Use tests, chromatography and instrumental ideas to identify substances from fully stated observations.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional results tables and safe classroom descriptions. Never instruct learners to handle hazardous chemicals.

objectives.text: Interpret qualitative analysis, chromatography and identification evidence.

units.title: Physics: energy
units.description: Explain energy stores, transfers, work, power, efficiency and conservation with calculations.
units.generationNotes: State formulae, values and units. Use fictional everyday systems and show each calculation step.

objectives.text: Use energy models and equations to explain transfers, work, power and efficiency.

units.title: Physics: electricity
units.description: Analyse circuits, current, potential difference, resistance, power and electrical energy.
units.generationNotes: Describe circuit arrangements in text and state every value. Use safe fictional calculations, not mains wiring instructions.

objectives.text: Use circuit models and equations to analyse electrical quantities and energy.

units.title: Physics: particle model
units.description: Use particles to explain density, states of matter, internal energy, pressure and changes of state.
units.generationNotes: Give all masses, volumes and temperatures. Avoid unseen diagrams and explain models as approximations.

objectives.text: Use the particle model to explain matter, density, pressure and energy changes.

units.title: Physics: atomic structure
units.description: Explain radiation, atomic structure, half-life, nuclear equations and uses and risks of radiation.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional sources and numerical data. Explain risk proportionately and do not give medical or operational advice.

objectives.text: Explain atomic structure and radioactive processes using evidence and equations.

units.title: Physics: forces
units.description: Apply force, motion, momentum, pressure and Newton's laws to fully specified situations.
units.generationNotes: State all masses, velocities and directions. Show vector reasoning in words when no diagram is supplied.

objectives.text: Use force and motion models to explain and calculate changes in movement and momentum.

units.title: Physics: waves
units.description: Describe wave properties and use models for sound, light, reflection, refraction and the electromagnetic spectrum.
units.generationNotes: Describe wave diagrams verbally and state values. Do not make claims about personal exposure or treatment.

objectives.text: Explain and apply wave properties to sound, light and electromagnetic radiation.

units.title: Physics: magnetism
units.description: Explain magnetic fields, electromagnets, motors and induction using clear field and force reasoning.
units.generationNotes: Use text descriptions for field arrangements. Keep activities conceptual and do not provide unsafe electrical construction instructions.

objectives.text: Explain magnetic fields and electromagnetic effects in motors and induction.

units.title: Physics: space
units.description: Describe the solar system, star life cycles, orbital motion and evidence about the universe.
units.generationNotes: Use accepted school-level models and clearly label estimates. Avoid presenting unsettled claims as facts.

objectives.text: Explain key structures, cycles and evidence in astronomy and space physics.

units.title: History: medicine through time
units.description: Explain how medical ideas and treatments changed from medieval to modern periods using causes, consequences and evidence.
units.generationNotes: Use short original source descriptions and dated context. Avoid present-day medical advice and distinguish evidence from interpretation.

objectives.text: Explain change, continuity, causes and consequences in the history of medicine.

units.title: History: crime and punishment
units.description: Trace how definitions of crime, policing and punishment changed over time and explain reasons for change.
units.generationNotes: Use fictionalised or public-domain source summaries. Avoid stereotyping groups and separate historical description from modern judgement.

objectives.text: Explain change and continuity in crime, punishment and law enforcement over time.

units.title: History: Elizabethan England
units.description: Study society, government, religion and challenges in Elizabethan England through evidence and historical reasoning.
units.generationNotes: Use concise original source summaries and dates. Do not assume one experience represented every social group.

objectives.text: Analyse society, government, religion and challenges in Elizabethan England using evidence.

units.title: History: the First World War
units.description: Explain causes, key developments and consequences of the First World War using chronology and evidence.
units.generationNotes: Use short source summaries and clearly stated dates. Distinguish long-term causes from triggers and avoid graphic detail.

objectives.text: Explain causes, developments and consequences of the First World War.

units.title: History: Weimar and Nazi Germany
units.description: Analyse political, economic and social change in Weimar and Nazi Germany with careful source evaluation.
units.generationNotes: Use concise historical summaries and avoid propaganda reproduction. Explain competing interpretations and the human consequences of policy.

objectives.text: Explain change and evaluate evidence about Weimar and Nazi Germany.

units.title: History: the Cold War
units.description: Explain superpower tensions, crises, change and the eventual end of the Cold War using chronology and causation.
units.generationNotes: Use short original source descriptions and precise dates. Distinguish perspective from fact and avoid present-day political claims.

objectives.text: Explain causes, developments and consequences of the Cold War using evidence.

units.title: Geography: tectonic hazards
units.description: Explain plate tectonics, earthquakes, volcanoes, impacts and responses using physical and human factors.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional data or named examples only when accurate and sourced. Avoid claiming one response fits every community.

objectives.text: Explain tectonic processes, hazards, impacts and responses.

units.title: Geography: weather hazards
units.description: Understand tropical storms, UK weather extremes, climate patterns and risk reduction strategies.
units.generationNotes: Use clearly labelled data and distinguish weather from climate. Avoid unsupported forecasts or safety instructions.

objectives.text: Explain weather hazards, their impacts and strategies for managing risk.

units.title: Geography: climate change
units.description: Explain evidence, causes, impacts and responses to climate change using systems and scale.
units.generationNotes: Use evidence summaries and distinguish measured evidence from projection. Avoid false balance and state uncertainty carefully.

objectives.text: Explain causes, evidence, impacts and responses to climate change.

units.title: Geography: ecosystems
units.description: Study tropical rainforests, cold environments, interdependence, opportunities and management challenges.
units.generationNotes: Use data and named processes with clear scale. Avoid treating communities or environments as uniform.

objectives.text: Explain ecosystem processes, opportunities, challenges and sustainable management.

units.title: Geography: river landscapes
units.description: Explain erosion, transport, deposition, river landforms, flooding and management choices.
units.generationNotes: Describe diagrams in words and provide all measurements. Compare hard and soft management without claiming a universal best option.

objectives.text: Explain river processes, landforms, flooding and management responses.

units.title: Geography: urban issues
units.description: Analyse urbanisation, city opportunities, challenges, inequalities and sustainability strategies.
units.generationNotes: Use fictional or accurately sourced city data. Avoid stereotypes and distinguish local evidence from generalisation.

objectives.text: Explain urbanisation, urban challenges, opportunities and sustainable strategies.

units.title: Geography: global development
units.description: Use indicators and development models to explain differences, causes, consequences and strategies for reducing the gap.
units.generationNotes: Use precise definitions and fictional data when possible. Avoid ranking people or places simplistically.

objectives.text: Use evidence and models to explain global development differences and responses.

units.title: Geography: resource management
units.description: Explore food, water and energy security, demand, distribution and sustainable management choices.
units.generationNotes: Use stated data and compare trade-offs. Avoid personal environmental prescriptions presented as universal facts.

objectives.text: Explain resource pressures, inequalities and sustainable management strategies.
